name: Ableton - Drift growl and wobble
description: Reference checklist for a native Ableton Drift growl: initialized saw and low-pass, Env 2 filter movement, audio-rate LFO pitch FM, inverse high-pass movement and Saturator. Not executable.

manual.instruction: Initialize Drift: turn oscillator 2 down, remove the filter frequency modulation, set Envelope 1 sustain to 100% and release to minimum, and set velocity-to-volume to 0%.
manual.verify: The synth is a clean saw through an open low-pass with no hidden modulation.
manual.why: Matt Tinkler starts from an initialized Drift so every later move is deliberate.

manual.instruction: Set the low-pass to about 20 Hz. Assign Envelope 2 to filter frequency, raise its attack, drop sustain to 0% and adjust decay until the filter opens and closes like a wub.
manual.verify: The filter moves slowly enough to hear as a growl rather than a pluck.
manual.why: Matt Tinkler uses Envelope 2 on the low-pass with a slow attack and zero sustain.

manual.instruction: Set Drift's LFO rate to 1:1 so it runs at audio rate relative to the oscillator. Apply a small amount of LFO to pitch and choose a whole-number ratio from 1 to 16.
manual.verify: The growl gains aggressive FM harmonics while remaining tonal.
manual.why: Matt Tinkler uses Drift's 1:1 LFO for pitch FM and recommends whole-number ratios.

manual.instruction: Assign Envelope 2 negatively to the high-pass frequency so it moves opposite the low-pass. Then assign Envelope 2 to the LFO amount for extra pitch movement.
manual.verify: The filter tone evolves through the note instead of sitting in one place.
manual.why: Matt Tinkler adds inverse high-pass movement and envelope-controlled LFO depth.

manual.instruction: Try oscillator shape changes, a second oscillator an octave or fifth above with detune, different filter types/resonance and different LFO waveforms. Raise oscillator level to drive the filter for saturation.
manual.verify: The patch has several distinct timbres without adding new devices.
manual.why: Matt Tinkler varies shape, oscillator layering, filter type and LFO waveform in Drift.

manual.instruction: Add Ableton Saturator after Drift, increase drive and try the Base Shape or Color modes. Finish with EQ and only a small amount of width or unison.
manual.verify: The growl is louder and more aggressive but still mono-compatible in the low end.
manual.why: Matt Tinkler uses Saturator's drive, Base Shape and Color, then discusses width and unison.

notes: Source: Matt Tinkler, 'Make AWESOME Bass Growls With Ableton Drift' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KQlGU3LTWMk). Transcript summary, not quotes. Reference-only because the engine cannot create or verify Drift patches.
